summary_paragraph: Mr. ___, a male with relapsed multiple myeloma, chronic hemolytic anemia, type 2 diabetes, and stage 3 chronic kidney disease, was admitted for weakness and confusion. He was found to have acute kidney injury on chronic kidney disease, with creatinine rising to 3.1 from a baseline of 2.1–2.3, and severe anemia with hemoglobin of 6.3 g/dL, for which he received two units of packed red blood cells. Imaging showed no source of bleeding, and his anemia was attributed to chronic disease and myeloma. One blood culture grew coagulase-negative Staphylococcus, identified as oxacillin-resistant Staphylococcus epidermidis, prompting treatment with intravenous vancomycin and a vancomycin port lock for a planned two-week course. Repeat cultures were negative, and echocardiogram showed no endocarditis. His mental status and weakness improved with transfusion and hydration. Urinary retention was noted with a post-void residual of 64 cc, managed with continued tamsulosin. He was discharged home with services on vancomycin, with plans to restart carfilzomib after oncology follow-up, and instructions to monitor weight and follow up on labs.
problems: Sepsis due to other specified staphylococcus
